resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: A pipeline corridor from Abqaiq/Shedgum (Eastern Province) west to Yanbu (Red Sea / Al Madinah) is heavily documented in independent sources, so a physical asset exists. The name and length are GEM-only artifacts. CLASSIFICATION (primary concern): the long-haul Abqaiq/Shedgum->Yanbu line of this scale is fundamentally an NGL pipeline, not a dry-gas transmission line. Techint (operator of record for the original line) describes the ~1,166 km Shedgum-Yanbu line built ~1978; Argaam, offshore-technology and the 2017 EIA all describe the Shedgum/Abqaiq->Yanbu line as carrying NGL/ethane as petrochemical feedstock for Jubail/Yanbu ('largest NGL pipeline' per EIA). The 585 km / 30 in figure cited by Argaam is the SHY-1 NGL expansion. None of these describe a dry-gas trunk of 966 km with diameters 42/48/56 in. So Fuel='Gas' is very likely a misclassification of an NGL line. DUPLICATE: GEM already separately tracks (a) the East-West Gas Pipeline Abqaiq->Yanbu as P3962 (1200 km, 48 in) and P3966 (821 km), and (b) a standalone 'Abqaiq-Yanbu NGL pipeline' wiki page. P1897's 966 km / 42,48,56 in overlaps that same Abqaiq->Yanbu corridor, so it is likely a relabel/segment double-count of one of those rather than a distinct fifth Abqaiq->Yanbu line. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=Saudi Aramco 100% is correct and well corroborated (Aramco/Techint/offshore-tech all attribute Abqaiq->Yanbu lines to Saudi Aramco) - that single field is fine. ENDPOINTS: StartLocation is blank in GEM; only StartCountry/EndCountry = Saudi Arabia are recorded - endpoints (Abqaiq/Shedgum -> Yanbu) are undocumented in the row and should be filled if the entity is retained. Net: do not silently pass. Treat as a classification + likely-duplicate concern pending a human decision on whether to reclassify to NGL, merge into P3962/P3966 or the NGL page, or delete as a GEM-only spurious entity.

resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: Confirmed real. 'UBTG' is a genuine Saudi Aramco corridor designation (Uthmaniyah-Berri Trunk Gas line), part of the Master Gas System. Independent, verifier-passing sources confirm the Aramco MGS as an extensive processed-gas trunk network connecting the Berri, Uthmaniyah, Hawiyah, Juaymah and Shedgum gas plants in the Eastern Province (OGN News; Saudipedia Hawiyah Gas Plant). The pipeline-specific characteristics (length 249 km, telescoping diameters 56/36/38/40/42 in) match a peer-reviewed paper titled 'Electromagnetic Interference Caused By A High Voltage Transmission Network On Buried Pipelines & Communication Cables' (ResearchGate publication 291522747), which contains a table literally titled 'UBTG-1 Pipeline Characteristics' and studies Aramco buried pipelines near the 380 kV Shedgum-Qurayyah lines in the Eastern Province. That paper is the apparent origin of GEM's numbers, but it is hosted only on ResearchGate/Academia.edu, both of which return HTTP 403 to scripts/url_verifier.py, so I cannot stage its URL. This is the ONLY independent confirmation of the exact specs, so the specs are at best medium and effectively single-sourced for citation purposes. NOT a hallucination, but the GEM-only-derived web echo is heavy: nearly all generic web hits ('249 km, diameters 56,36,38,40,42, Saudi Aramco') trace straight back to gem.wiki. CLASSIFICATION: Correctly a dry/sales GAS transmission trunk line, not NGL and not a gathering line - the Master Gas System carries processed sales gas (OGN, Saudipedia). Fuel=Gas confirmed; Owner=Saudi Aramco confirmed (whole MGS is Aramco-owned/operated). DUPLICATE CONCERN (see separate validity object): P1899 'UBTG-1-Berri 2' is 247 km with the identical diameter set - almost certainly the parallel/twin line of the same corridor or a double-count of one telescoping pipe; flagged below.

GEM has additionally fragmented the corridor into km-marker rows (P1900 UBTG-km56-AY-1 KP916, P1910/P1911 UBTG-1-km0-UBTG-1-km56 [a '1' and a '2'], P1912 Hawiyah-UBTG-1-km0). The name decodes to a route-segment descriptor, not a reportable named pipeline: 'UBTG' = Uthmaniyah-Berri-Tanajib-Ghawar gas network (part of Saudi Aramco's Master Gas System; this much IS independently attested via MEED/Aramco/pipeline-journal coverage of the UBTG and MGS systems), 'km56' = kilometer 56 on the UBTG-1 line, and 'AY-1 KP916' = kilometer-post 916 on the Abqaiq-Yanbu Oil Line I (AY-1) crude line (offshore-technology.com confirms Abqaiq-Yanbu Oil Line I: 1,204 km, up to 56-inch, Eastern Province->Al Madinah, crude oil, operating since 1987). So the GEM row describes a gas segment running from km56 of the UBTG line to KP916 (a point alongside the crude AY-1 corridor). Web searches in English (and the broad MGS/UBTG literature) return the segment name 'UBTG-km56-AY-1 KP916' ONLY on gem.wiki itself and GEM-derived echoes; no media, Aramco, SPA, Argaam, or trade source independently reports this segment, its 244 km length, its 56-inch diameter, or its endpoints. The two refs attached to the gem.wiki page are generic OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletins (ASB2012 PDF, ASB2013 p.79) that report only aggregate Saudi pipeline statistics, not this individual line. I verified the ASB2012 PDF returns HTTP 200 but it does NOT contain segment-specific 'pipeline' content matching this row (url_verifier FAIL on token 'pipeline'); the ASB2013 flipbook page returns HTTP 403. Net: the underlying UBTG/MGS network and the Aramco ownership are real and the gas-commodity classification is plausible, but THIS specific kilometer-post-named segment is a GEM-only entity with no independent corroboration of existence or specs — consistent with extraction from a route/GIS dataset that sliced a trunk line into KP-labeled segments (cf. sibling rows P1910/P1911/P1912 'UBTG-1-km0-UBTG-1-km56' and P1903 'AY-1 KP 943-Riyadh', which share the same artificial KP-naming pattern and may be co-slices of the same physical infrastructure). resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: The UBTG (Uthmaniyah-Berri Transmission Gas) system is real Aramco infrastructure - independent sources confirm UBTG-3 (152 km, Uthmaniyah->Juaymah/Berri) and UBTG-4 (Shedgum->Ju'aymah, built by Saipem, confirmed by ETE Readymix contractor page). So the corridor physically exists. HOWEVER, no independent source confirms a discrete pipeline entity named 'UBTG-1km-Juanymah' of 204 km. PROVENANCE: The whole GEM UBTG-* family (P1898-P1900, P1910-P1912 and this row) traces to a ResearchGate table titled 'UBTG-1 Pipeline Characteristics' (figure tbl3, paper 291522747) - an academic pipeline-integrity/corrosion study that segments the single UBTG-1 line by kilometer markers (km0, km56, etc.). 'UBTG-1km-Juanymah' reads as the UBTG-1 segment terminating at Juaymah, i.e. a waypoint slice of ONE corridor, not a standalone pipe. That ResearchGate page is 403-blocked to automated fetch so I could not read the numbers directly. CITATIONS PROBLEM: the two refs on the gem.wiki page (OPEC ASB2012 p.75; ASB2013 p.79) do NOT support this row - url_verifier confirms ASB2012.pdf returns 200 but contains no occurrence of 'pipeline'; ASB pages are generic annual statistics bulletins, not pipeline-specific. So the entity currently rests only on the (inaccessible) integrity-study table plus GEM-derived material. SPEC: 204 km and diameters 28/30/38/40 in could not be independently corroborated; the mixed 4-value diameter set is itself consistent with a multi-segment corridor rather than a single pipe of one bore. CLASSIFICATION CAVEAT: Juaymah is principally an NGL fractionation/LPG export terminal; MEED reporting describes the KGP->Juaymah feed as a 24-in 103-km NGL line and Aramco material describes liquids being piped to Ju'aymah for fractionation. The 'UBTG' name implies transmission (dry) gas, so I keep commodity as a caveat rather than a hard reclassification, but a reviewer should confirm whether this Juaymah-bound segment carries dry gas vs NGL. ATTRIBUTION: Owner Saudi Aramco 100% is safe (entire MGS/UBTG network is Aramco). Endpoints in GEM are blank except country=Saudi Arabia; from the corridor it is plausibly an Uthmaniyah-area node to Juaymah, but no source confirms this specific segment's endpoints, so I did not stage them. VERDICT: concern - primary = duplicate/segmentation (km-point slice of UBTG-1 likely double-counting corridor length), secondary = unverifiable spec and a citation set that does not actually support the row.

resolutions.recommendation: If P1902 is not deleted as a duplicate of P1958, verify whether it is really a gas line at all; Safaniya field associated gas does NOT travel via a dedicated 198 km trunk to Ju'aymah -- it is gathered to Safaniya GOSP-1 / Tanajib and sent along the coast to Berri/Shedgum/Ju'aymah processing. resolutions.researcher_notes: CLASSIFICATION/EXISTENCE-AS-RECORDED doubt. The independent Fluor 'Aramco Offshore Gas Gathering Plant' description (primary EPC contractor) details the actual Safaniya/Marjan/Zuluf associated-gas routing: Safaniya GOSP-2/3/4 gas is compressed offshore and sent to Safaniya GOSP-1 ONSHORE 'for further handling', Marjan gas goes to Tanajib, Zuluf gas to Safaniya; recovered gas then travels 'along the coast to processing facilities at Berri, Shedgum and Ju'aymah' over 'more than 150 miles of various diameter pipelines, primarily offshore.' That is a gathering network feeding multiple plants -- NOT a single 198 km dry-gas transmission trunk from Safaniya to Ju'aymah. Ju'aymah's own gas role is an NGL fractionation plant fed by the NGL system from Shedgum/Uthmaniyah, not by a raw-gas line from Safaniya. So even if a Safaniya-related gas line exists, recording it as a 198 km / 40-in Safaniya->Ju'aymah dry-gas transmission pipeline misrepresents the documented system (it is either the crude trunk P1958, or part of the offshore gathering network, not a 198 km gas trunk). No independent source corroborates the 40-in diameter or the 198 km length for a GAS line.

WHAT IS CORROBORATED (context, not the entity): The broader physical corridor IS real and Aramco-owned. The Master Gas System (developed from 1975, operational 1982) 'crosses from Yanbu on the Red Sea to Shedgum and passes by Riyadh' and was built to deliver gas to central-region power stations (MEED 'Master Gas System' page, verified). Since the MGS explicitly transmits processed gas to Riyadh-area power plants, dry-gas classification is defensible, but cannot be independently confirmed for THIS row.

Net: real corridor, but this specific named entity and all its specs (153 km, 48 in) trace only to GEM/OPEC — do not rubber-stamp.

The OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2017, Table 9.9 'Main gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2016' (p.136), Saudi Arabia section, lists 'Abqaiq/Shedgum - Saudi Aramco - 33 [miles] - 42 [inches]'. The ASB 2012 edition (Saudi gas pipelines table) lists the same line as 'Abqaiq-B/Shedgum - Saudi Aramco - 33 - 42' - the '-B' node label is exactly the source of GEM's name 'Abqaiq-B-Shedgum'. Both confirmed by direct pypdf text extraction of the PDFs (the wiki had cited these two ASB editions; the verifier reads r.text and cannot parse PDF tables, so it FAILs the token check on any PDF even when the token is genuinely present - URL resolution is OK/200 for both). CLASSIFICATION: CONFIRMED gas transmission line - it sits in the natural-gas pipelines table (Table 9.9), Saudi Aramco operator, NOT in the crude (6.9), product (6.10), or NGL tables; commodity 'Gas' is correct. Abqaiq and Shedgum are both major Aramco gas-processing complexes in the Eastern Province roughly 30-40 km apart, so a 53 km gas trunk between them is geographically coherent and consistent with the dense Abqaiq/Shedgum/Uthmaniyah/Hawiyah gas network. DUPLICATE: none - the ASB Saudi gas table maps 1:1 onto the GEM roster (UBTG-1/Berri to P1898/P1899, Abqaiq/Berri to P1906, Aindar/Shedgum to P1924, Depco/Abqaiq to P1925, etc.); P1913 is the single 'Abqaiq/Shedgum' row. No other roster row is the same physical pipe (P1924 Aindar-Shedgum is a different origin, 34 km, 12 in). SPEC: Diameter 42 in matches exactly; Length GEM 53.00 km = 33 miles in the ASB (33 mi = 53.1 km - GEM's value is the direct metric conversion); Owner Saudi Aramco matches; FuelSource 'Abqaiq' = start node, consistent; endpoints Abqaiq->Shedgum, Eastern Province, both confirmed. Capacity is genuinely blank - no independent figure found; left blank rather than fabricated. CAVEAT: the two corroborating references are two editions of the same OPEC publication, so this is one strong source lineage rather than two fully independent origins; no non-OPEC source gives this granular segment's specs (segment too fine for press coverage). Treated as medium-high single-family corroboration. Also note the wiki's own cited URLs (opec.org/opec_web/.../ASB2017_13062017.pdf and ASB2012.pdf) are now link-rotted - they 301-redirect to opec.org and then 403; recoverable only via the Wayback snapshots cited below.

Both sources are explicit that sweet gas comes from the Haradh, Ghazal, Wudayhi, Waqr and Tinat fields (Unayzah formation), while KHUFF (sour) gas comes ONLY from the Haradh field. The Waqr leg is a SWEET-gas feeder, so calling it a 'Khuff' line is wrong — the Khuff designation belongs to the Haradh-field lines (cf. roster siblings P1917/18/19 'Haradh Khuff-Hawiyah'). Also note this is a field-manifold-to-plant GATHERING/feeder line; sources do label them 'transmission lines,' so the gathering-vs-transmission framing is defensible, but it is not an MGS trunk line. NOT A DUPLICATE: distinct from P1920 'Tinat Kuff-Haradh' (Tinat manifold, 43 km, 20 in) by endpoint and diameter, and from P1917-19 (Haradh Khuff -> Hawiyah, different destination). resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: Ain Dar and Shedgum are both confirmed adjacent subfields of the Ghawar oil-and-gas field (independently corroborated: Saudipedia, NS Energy, CSEG/GeoExpro), roughly consistent with a ~34 km separation. So this is not a GEM-only / hallucinated entity. CLASSIFICATION: gas transmission is correct - it is a gas EXPORT pipeline carrying spare/associated gas from the Wafra Joint Operations (the partitioned-neutral-zone heavy-oil operation jointly run by Kuwait Gulf Oil Co. and Saudi Arabian Chevron) to KOC's gas booster station BS-171, which processes dry/conditioned export gas; not an NGL line, not a gathering line. ATTRIBUTION CAVEATS (not blocking but should be corrected): (a) GEM Owner = 'Kuwait Petroleum Corp 100%' but every source names the project owner/client as Kuwait Oil Company (KOC), KPC's upstream subsidiary - KOC is the more precise owner/operator. Note: this row sits in the Saudi gas roster but is physically a Kuwait/Neutral-Zone pipeline owned by a Kuwaiti operator - geographically a Kuwait asset, though the feed (Wafra JO) is jointly Saudi/Kuwaiti, so its placement in the Saudi sweep is defensible. No duplicate found in the 65-row Saudi gas roster.

resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED. The Hasbah-to-Wasit gas pipeline is real and independently documented. Oil & Gas Journal (24 Mar 2016) reports Aramco commissioned the offshore Hasbah field, part of the two-field Al Wasit gas project, and that 'Twin 36-in. trunklines will carry production from the fields to the Wasit gas plant.' Offshore-Technology's Al Wasit Gas Program and Hasbah Gas Field Expansion pages independently describe a 36in-diameter export pipeline from the Hasbah tie-in platforms to the Wasit gas plant. These are separate origins, not GEM-derived. CLASSIFICATION: CONFIRMED as a dry-gas transmission trunkline (non-associated sour gas from Hasbah to the onshore Wasit processing plant; NGL is extracted downstream at the plant, so the trunkline itself is correctly gas/transmission). FuelSource = Hasbah Gas Field: CONFIRMED. Owner = Aramco 100%: CONFIRMED (wholly Aramco mega-project). Diameter = 36 in: CONFIRMED HIGH by 3 independent sources (OGJ 'Twin 36-in. trunklines'; Offshore-Technology Al Wasit '36in in diameter'; Offshore-Technology Hasbah Expansion '36in-diameter pipeline'). DUPLICATE: P7766 (Pipeline 1) and P7767 (Pipeline 2), both 80 km / 36 in, plausibly correspond to the documented TWIN trunklines, so they are most likely two genuine parallel lines rather than a relabel double-count -- but this should be confirmed; if GEM intends them as the twin pair, that is consistent with sources. SPEC CONCERNS: (1) Capacity 1.00 MMcf/d is almost certainly an erroneous placeholder -- the Al Wasit program processes 2.5 bscfd (2,500 MMcf/d) combined Hasbah+Arabiyah; a single 36-in offshore trunkline carries on the order of 1+ bscf/d, not 1 MMcf/d. Recommend blanking or correcting. (2) StartYear1 = 2017 conflicts with independent sources: Wasit plant came onstream Oct 2015, Hasbah first gas reported Oct 2015/March 2016 (OGJ commissioning 24 Mar 2016; Argaam/Offshore-Energy 'Aramco starts gas production at Hasbah field'). The feeder trunkline was operational by 2015-2016, so 2017 is 1-2 years late. (3) LengthKnown = 80 km is not cleanly corroborated: Offshore-Technology's Hasbah Expansion page gives the Hasbah-Wasit 36-in line as ~36 km carbon-steel + 1.9 km CRA (~38 km); the Al Wasit program page cites a 260 km export pipeline plus a 120 km onshore pipeline; field is ~150 km NE of Jubail. None of these is 80 km, so the GEM length should be re-derived. Diameter/status/owner/fuel/type are solid; length, capacity, and start year are the weak points.

resolutions.researcher_notes: STRONGEST CONCERN = duplicate. P7768 'Abu Ali-Berri Gas Pipeline' (Al Jubail->Berri Gas Plant; len 22 km, dia 30 in, cap 220 MMcf/d, StartYear 2008, FuelSource Abu Ali Island, owner Saudi Aramco) is near-identical to roster row P1921 'Abu Ali-Berri Gas Pipeline' (Abu Ali Island->Berri Gas Plant; len 44 km, dia 30 in, cap 220 MMcf/d, StartYear 2008, FuelSource Abu Ali Island, owner Saudi Aramco). They share the SAME name, diameter (30 in), capacity (220 MMcf/d), start year (2008), fuel source, endpoint, owner, AND the SAME (now-dead) ref URL (steel-network.com). The ONLY differences are length (22 vs 44 km) and P7768's segment_name 'Sub-sea Pipeline'. This reads as one physical 30-in Abu Ali Island<->Berri line double-entered (likely a route split into an onshore + sub-sea leg, or a straight relabel). The reverse-direction P1922 (dia 8) / P1923 (dia 10) 'Berri-Abu Ali' rows belong to the same corridor cluster. EXISTENCE: the corridor itself is real and independently attested - Saipem 'Berri Downstream Pipeline' scope and NS Energy / GCS Contracting describe offshore pipelines (incl. a 30-in line) connecting Aramco's Abu Ali Island processing plant to Berri/Khursaniyah/Juaymah - so this is NOT a hallucinated entity. CLASSIFICATION CAVEAT: independent sources describe the Abu Ali<->Berri downstream lines as carrying stabilized Arabian light crude oil and sour condensate (crude/condensate service), not dry transmission gas; the gas/transmission classification is not independently confirmed for this specific route and may be mis-commodity. SPEC: the 22 km / 30 in / 220 MMcf/d / 2008 figures are GEM-only - the single cited non-GEM ref (steel-network.com) now 301-redirects to a steel-industry news homepage that contains NO Abu Ali/Berri/pipeline content (link rot), and web 'confirmations' of '22 km, 30 in, 2008' trace straight back to gem.wiki. OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletins cited on the wiki report country-level pipeline capacity, not this individual line. Net: real corridor, but this row is a probable duplicate of P1921 with GEM-only, uncorroborated specs and an unverified gas classification.
